author: fester
body: Arity resolution stays FIRST-match even though offset resolution is last-match: runtime helpers are recorded with arity zero on purpose and the dispatch is calibrated to that answer (the ARM64 chapter carries the measurement).

author: fester
body: rv-bind-local appends and rv-lookup-local reads the last match, so a scope is a suffix of st.locals: entering one adds bindings at the end, leaving one has to drop them again. What is saved is the LENGTH, not the list. __list_push writes into the same buffer and hands back the same pointer whenever capacity allows, so holding the old field value and putting it back changes nothing -- it only ever appeared to work when a bind hit the grow path and got a fresh buffer. act-let-scope is the guard.

author: fester
body: A zero-argument effect operation goes through the handler table ONLY when a handler was installed: an unwritten slot reads zero and calling through it dies before the first print, which is what `console-readline-cite` did on this lane too (the ARM64 chapter carries the account). An unhandled `read-line` answers the None cell.

author: fester
body: A unit type is runtime-transparent: its representation IS the inner type, so every dispatch that picks an instruction sequence by type must see through the wrapper. Before the UnitTy arms here, a compare on a `unit Real` took the integer path, `show` on a `unit Text` printed the pointer, and a literal pattern on one never matched (measured 2026-07-28: unit-real-compare, unit-show, unit-pattern-lit).

author: fester
body: A simple expression is one whose evaluation cannot disturb a value already staged in an argument register. Literals qualify because they lower to a single load-immediate. A name qualifies only when it resolves to a local or a parameter, which lives in a callee-saved register or a spill slot and is reached with a load.

author: fester
body: Answering False when unsure is free: it buys a save and a reload. Answering True when unsure returns a wrong number.

author: fester
body: **This is not the general fix and must not be read as one.** Two live temporaries either side of a binop can still collide in frameless mode, here and in `rv-emit-frameless-binop-reg`; what is fixed is the shape that occurs, where one side is a literal. The general defect is open and is not fixed here.
